text_span: Our contributions are threefold:
We construct a family of Fourier–Markov operators that integrate spectral decomposition with stochastic transition probabilities, grounded in the principles of discrete-time quantum walks.

By mapping random walk processes into a quantum-inspired Hilbert space, our method captures both frequency-domain characteristics and probabilistic evolution, enabling interpretable and scalable modular partitions.

We evaluate the proposed framework on synthetic and real-world dynamic networks, demonstrating superior performance in terms of modularity maximization, temporal stability, and robustness compared to state-of-the-art baselines.
